newsitem.title: INDIA: India to invest in infrastructure finance firm.
newsitem.headline: India to invest in infrastructure finance firm.

text.p: The Indian cabinet on Wednesday approved an investment of 5.0 billion rupees by the government to start an Infrastructure Development Finance Company (IDFC), the government said.

Authorities said that the government, the Reserve Bank of India, banks and financial institutions will own stakes in IDFC, which is expected to arrange financing for costly, long-term infrastructure projects.
"Approval for contribution during 1996/97 (April-March) by government is to an extent of 5.0 billion rupees which would include equity and quasi equity/loan in the IDFC," the statement said.

India, which opened up its infrastructure sector to private and foreign investors under an economic reform programme launched in 1991, is seeking funds worth billions of dollars for key projects to push the economy to a high-growth path. "The main purpose of establishing IDFC includes providing financial and non-financial support in financing infrastructure projects in the power, telecommunications, roadways, ports, airports, industrial parks, water supply, sanitation, waterways, urban transport systems and railways," the government said in a statement.
IDFC, to be established with an authorised capital of 50 billion rupees, will function outside the government sector with an independent board of directors, the statement said.

"To begin with, the company will be capitalised with an amount of 16 billion rupees of which 10 billion rupees would paid-up equity and 6.0 billion rupees would be long-term subordinated debt," the statement said.
The capital of 16 billion would enable IDFC to leverage its resources through debt to around 100 billion rupees over the first few years of its operation, the statement said.

The statement said the government, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and state-run financial institutions will together hold up to 40 percent in IDFC, while the rest of the equity would be held by domestic and overseas institutional investors.

However, as finalisation of overseas investment would take some time, domestic institutional investors will initially hold all of the 60 percent of IDFC's equity outside the government, the statement said.
The government and RBI will subscribe 3.0 billion rupees each to the long-term subordinated debt of 6.0 billion rupees for a period of 15 years, it said.
"The interest rate on this loan shall be equivalent to the rate at which dividend is paid on equity shares in the relevant year," the statement said.
